lectures.title: Converting the Image String to a File

cues.en: To emit this image, I of course want to use my image pick custom event and I actually want to allow
to either emit a string here or what you can do by adding one pipe here,
a file, file is a default Javascript type.
Now of course, we do convert our image here to a base64 string and so we could emit that string here, wouldn't
be wrong,
it would work but later, we haven't added this yet but later, we will actually convert that base64 string
to a file that we can upload.
We need to do this for the camera where we get such a base64 string,
here we already get a file,
so converting it to a string and then converting it back sounds a bit redundant.
So therefore here, I want to emit my picked file with the image pick event here, just like that,
so I want emit picked file here without errors.
And now we're doing that,
now we're emitting a file picked through the file picker as well,
the next step is now to continue with that in the new offer page and there of course, we're receiving
that imageData and that no longer is just a string,
it could also be a file of course.
Therefore here in on image pick in the new offer component where we get either a string which is
this base64 URL or where we get the file, I first of all have to check the type of imageData and
if that is a string, I want to do something, else I want to do something else because else, it's a file
and if it's a file, I don't need to convert it. If it is a string, I need to convert it to a file though.
Now to make that conversion, we'll use a utility function which you find attached to this video.
You can just paste it here into your component file above the @component decorator below your imports,
this is a function that will basically convert a base64 string as we're getting it to a blob which in the
end is a file. So you can just copy that in,
don't need to change anything there and in onImagePicked, here if we have such a base64 string which
we need to convert, you can now call base64toBlob and pass your imageData in there.
Now important, it won't work like that,
instead you need to call replace on that imageData string and replace a string, which is
data:image/jpg;base64, with nothing
because this basically is a prefix that the images generated by the camera plugin will have
and this basically turns it into an invalid base64 string that can be converted by this method,
so we have to remove it which is what we're doing here.
The
base64toBlob method here also requires a second argument and that is the content type and that will
always be image.jpg because the Capacitor camera plugin gives you jpg images.
So now this gives us a file but of course we want to store that file somewhere and I'll store it in
my image file property here and it is a good idea to also wrap this with a try block so that in case
this conversion fails for whatever reason, we can catch the error and then do something with it here.
So for example, throw an alert and inform the user that this image can't be used and that he
should choose another one for example but for us, this should really work in this app here.
Still, good idea to provide a fallback or handle the error somehow.
Now that is the case that we're getting such a base64 string,
if we are getting a file, so an image file, then we don't really need to do anything too fancy with it, we
can just use it as it is because and that is now the next thing, I want to add a new control here on our
form.
We do have that location control which we added, now I'll add an image control here which is a new form control
and the initial value here should be null
and here I also will not set any validators but it should just be a form control like that
and now when we picked an image, I want to set that image to that image control.
Therefore in onImagePicked, I'll actually not initialize a constant image file here but a variable,
let imageFile and then this either is the result of my conversion here or in the else block, image file
is imageData because the imageData then is a file so that after this if check here, we can just call
this form patch value and set that image control we just added to our image file because we can store
that file in our control as well.
And now we have that file stored and we can now work on the form submission and see what we do with
that file.
